I was content with this dog training school until my most recent experience with customer service.

I’ve driven 45–60 minutes each way to attend classes and socials at their Yonge & Eglinton, Etobicoke, and Dundas locations because I’m highly committed to my puppy’s development and liked all the good reviews. I have a German Shepherd and early training and socialization is very important for this breed.

I originally purchased a package that included Puppy Start Right and Foundation Skills 1. I have just completed Puppy Start Right and the 5 socials that are included in the package. Recently, I found out that I need to temporarily relocate for work and will be bringing my puppy with me. Because of that, I contacted When Hounds Fly to request a refund for the unused portion of my classes. I explained that dog training is expensive, and since I’m committed to continuing her training without interruption, I’ll need to enroll her in another school in the city that I’m moving to. Spending another $600–$700 on training, on top of moving expenses is not realistic for many people.

Their response was to refer me to their refund policy stating I have until March 2027 to use the classes, along with options to take courses remotely or transfer the credits to advanced classes. They also offered to waive the evaluation fee for advanced courses.

The problem is that these alternatives completely miss the point. Puppy training and socialization are most valuable during a very specific developmental window. Delaying classes for what could be 1-4 months, or replacing in-person puppy training with remote options, is not equivalent to what I originally paid for. The most reasonable solution would have been a refund for the unused services so I could continue her training immediately in my new city.

I was also told that classes are staffed and planned according to enrollment numbers. However, in my experience, class sizes vary dramatically. I’ve attended sessions with only one other dog and others that were completely full. Since these credits are valid for such a long period of time, it’s difficult to believe that one customer requesting a refund for unused future classes could meaningfully impact staffing or scheduling.

Unfortunately, the inflexibility and lack of empathy from management during a legitimate life circumstance left me disappointed.

I recently attended a seminar at When Hounds Fly about reactivity in dogs and how to manage it through clicker training — and it was a game changer.

The session started with an engaging theory segment, where we learned what goes on in a dog’s mind that makes them reactive, and the practical steps handlers can take to help their dogs stay calm and settle instead of barking or lunging at others. The slides and explanations made everything click (no pun intended)!

After the theory, the instructor demonstrated the techniques in a real-world walk with a reactive dog — which made it so much easier to understand how to apply the methods in everyday situations.

What I also really appreciated was the virtual seminar they send afterward by email. It’s a fantastic resource that helps review and strengthen everything we learned during class, offering an even more in-depth look at the concepts and techniques covered in the live seminar.

When I brought what I learned home and practiced it with Francisco, the 1½-year-old Chihuahua I dog-sit four days a week, the results were incredible. In just one month of consistent training, I noticed a huge difference in his behaviour — far less barking to “protect his space,” and much more calm, confident walking around other dogs.

I’ve also started applying the same teachings with my 4-year-old Cavapoo, who tends to react to bikes, and I’m already seeing real progress. These methods truly work across different personalities and triggers.

This seminar helped me deeply understand what’s happening in a reactive dog’s mind, how to read their body language, and how to redirect their responses in ways that make sense to them. Both Francisco and my Cavapoo are happier and more relaxed on our walks now — and so am I!

I can’t recommend When Hounds Fly enough for anyone who wants to build real understanding and better communication with their dog.
